title: Hybrid tensor-slice collective scheduler with staged kernel handoff and KV-affinity
author: Aisha Kapoor
description: Motivation: reduce multi-GPU tail latency and unnecessary small-tensor collectives during autoregressive generation. Implements a hybrid tensor-slice scheduler that stages a compute->collective kernel handoff, a tensor coalescer for adjacent small slices, and a KV-cache affinity layer to pin hot shards. Addresses operational pain points: token-latency spikes from scatter/gather ordering, redundant NCCL launches for sub-threshold slices, and cross-node KV churn from cache eviction storms. Key behaviors: delay collective launch until contiguous slice bytes exceed a threshold, handoff API to signal buffer readiness between streams via events, safe coalescing when tensors share layout and lifetime, and per-shard affinity metadata with eviction hysteresis for the cache manager. Continuous-batcher hooks allow affinity-aware batching to prefer requests that can reuse device-local KV prefixes. All changes are behind runtime flags and include calibrated defaults per GPU-profile. Benchmarks: 8xA100 multi-node TP conv-dialog workload shows median token latency -13.8% (beam=1), 22% fewer small NCCL launches, and 9% less cross-node KV traffic. Backwards compatibility preserved by defaults and feature flags. Linked Linear: ENG-1427, PERF-88. Checklist: scheduler design doc reviewed; unit+integration tests; perf harness; runtime feature flag; docs/telemetry updated.

review_conversation: Miguel Santos: Nice design; can you clarify the handoff memory fencing? The ordering looked racy in the initial patch.

Aisha Kapoor: The handoff uses a cudaEvent-based fence on the compute stream before we allow the collective stream to reuse the buffer; I added an explicit device synchronize in the fix commit and a unit test that repros the previous race.
Celine Park: Can we expose the grouping threshold as a runtime knob? We should avoid hardcoding for different hardware generations.
Aisha Kapoor: Added runtime flag scheduler.tensor_slice_group_threshold and a calibrated default per-GPU profile in runtime/profiles/; documented behavior in the RFC.
Danielle Wu: Perf numbers look good; please add an A/B for KV-eviction policy to ensure long-tail stateful sessions aren't affected.
Aisha Kapoor: Added eviction hysteresis and an opt-in linear task PERF-88 to evaluate in canary. Updated benchmark harness to measure tail p99s.
Miguel Santos: Approve after minor nits are addressed.
release_notes: Introduce hybrid tensor-slice scheduler with staged compute->collective kernel handoff, NCCL small-tensor coalescing, and KV-cache affinity to reduce cross-node traffic and small-collective overhead. Feature is opt-in via runtime flags. Expect reduced token latency on TP workloads and fewer small NCCL launches.
notes: Runtime flags: scheduler.enable_tensor_slice_handoff, scheduler.tensor_slice_group_threshold, kv.affinity_eviction_hysteresis. Monitoring: scheduler.handoff_count, scheduler.grouped_nccl_ops, kv.affinity_local_hits. Canary plan: enable on dedicated-tp canaries with low traffic and observe p50/p95/p99 for 72h before broader rollout.
